transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-02 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC; Duration ~52m; Attendees listed above.

Summary (auto): quick scoping to align on pilot goals, determine sample workload and infra constraints, agree on benchmark plan and next steps.

00:00 Maya Delgado: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to make this a focused scoping session — maybe 45, 50 minutes — to nail down success criteria and the integration path.
00:12 Evan Torres: sounds good, maya, i'll try to keep it high level, priya and samir will dig into the infra bits.
00:18 Maya Delgado: perfect. quick intros? real quick.
00:22 Priya Nair: priya, lead ml, we own the summarization model stack, mostly open-source checkpoints, running on k8s.
00:26 Samir Gupta: samir, platform eng — we manage the gpu fleet and the vpn/vpc peering stuff.
00:30 Ravi Shah: ravi from redwood se — i'll own the benchmark setup and run the initial tests.
00:35 Jordan Lee: jordan pm, i'm owner of the alerting use case.
00:40 Lina Park: lina from solutions — here to map integration choices and SDK questions.
00:45 Evan Torres: ok, first, what's the core thing we want to validate in the pilot?
00:50 Maya Delgado: good Q — high level: 1) integration ergonomics with your stack (SDK or OpenAI-compat endpoints), 2) latency and throughput under representative traffic, 3) structured output/tool calling reliability for downstream parsers, and 4) cost per unit at target quantization/batching.
01:05 Priya Nair: on structured output, we need consistent JSON blocks for entity extraction, low hallucination on keys like "severity" and "timestamp". So we need a stability metric.
01:15 Ravi Shah: noted, we can run a schema-accuracy eval and provide a regression alert if structure deviates beyond X%. we usually recommend a test set of ~300 canonical prompts.
01:26 Samir Gupta: traffic profile — currently peak 250 rps for summarization pipeline during business hours, long tail down to 5 rps off-hours. avg tokens per call ~600 with bursts to 2k for long docs.
01:40 Jordan Lee: latency target is tough — we want user-facing summaries under 200ms p50 ideally, p95 under 600ms. but that's with our current on-prem infra; we are open to dedicated capacity.
01:55 Maya Delgado: thanks, samir, that's helpful. quick sanity check: for 600 token avg that's tighter, p50 200ms is aggressive. we should split success tiers: "baseline" (hosted Redwood API, p50 < 400ms) and "stretch" (Dedicated + optimizations, p50 < 200ms).
02:13 Evan Torres: yeah that tiering makes sense. cost target? we have an internal threshold, trying to keep inference cost under $0.002 normalized token — otherwise product margins get hit.
02:25 Lina Park: we can model cost tradeoffs: batching, kv cache for prefixes, and 8-bit quantization all reduce unit cost but change latency. we'll include a config matrix.
02:36 Priya Nair: also curious about function/tool calling — we want the model to choose which extractor to call, and then call our internal enrichment service. is Redwood's function calling identical to OpenAI's?
02:48 Ravi Shah: it's OpenAI-compat for payloads and function schema; semantics are similar but there are small differences in wiring for streaming. we have examples in the SDK for wiring tool responses back into the message loop. sometimes the names of fields get normalized differently in transcripts, so watch for that.
03:05 Samir Gupta: network/security — we need to know if pilot will require VPC peering, private control plane, or if hosted endpoints (TLS + mTLS) suffice for initial tests. we have KMS and specific audit log retention needs.
03:20 Maya Delgado: right. for initial bench we can start on hosted Redwood API (TLS) to accelerate time-to-first-result, then move to a Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering if you need KMS in your control plane. send the KMS requirements and we'll map to our Private checklist.
03:36 Evan Torres: how long for the pilot? what's realistic?
03:39 Maya Delgado: we typically do a 6-week pilot: week 0 onboarding + infra, week1 baseline runs, week2 optimization (batching/quant), week3 tool calling/structured output tuning, week4 reliability runs + A/B logic, week5 SLA checks and a handoff doc. we can compress to 4 weeks if you want a smaller scope.
04:00 Jordan Lee: let's tentatively agree to 6 weeks, but we might compress the baseline if we can run parallel tests.
04:07 Priya Nair: benchmarks — what metrics will you capture?
04:10 Ravi Shah: we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (rps), tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, schema accuracy for structured output, failure modes (timeouts, function mis-invocations), and retry rates. we'll publish raw traces to the harness and a summarized dashboard in Redwood Console.
04:30 Priya Nair: good. will you run both SDK integration and OpenAI-compat endpoints? we prefer the OpenAI-compat because we have tooling built around it.
04:40 Lina Park: we recommend starting with the OpenAI-compat layer for minimal code change — your current client will drop in with small wiring changes. SDK gives more telemetry out of the box and easier streaming control; both are possible in the pilot.
04:54 Samir Gupta: about streaming — we need chunked events for progressive UI updates. is that available over the compat endpoint?
04:58 Ravi Shah: yes, we support streaming over the OpenAI-compatible API; the SDK is a little more ergonomic for websocket/stream handling but the compat endpoints do stream as well. sometimes the event chunk keys differ.
05:12 Evan Torres: Priya mentioned schema accuracy. do you have tooling for deterministic structured outputs? we've seen models fluctuate even with system prompts.
05:20 Ravi Shah: two approaches: 1) constrained decoding + function calling (force calls to match schema), 2) post-parse validation with a regenerative loop for corrections. we'll include both in the harness; function calling + strict JSON schema usually gives the highest pass rate.
05:36 Priya Nair: ok, for the sample we will label expected keys and edge cases. you said 300 prompts — is that enough?
05:41 Ravi Shah: 300 canonical + 200 edge cases is a good start. during pilot we can expand.
05:47 Jordan Lee: what about long-context and kv cache? our summarization uses a sliding window with partial cache.
05:54 Lina Park: Redwood's KV cache supports prefix caching for repeated contexts and is beneficial when you have repeated system prompts or similar document headers. we'll map your sliding window pattern to caching hints to avoid regen costs.
06:06 Samir Gupta: any special infra requirements for the harness? we prefer a dockerized harness that runs in our cluster for encrypted traffic tests.
06:14 Ravi Shah: yes, we can provide a containerized harness that runs inside your environment; it will call either hosted endpoints or a Private control plane depending on the pilot phase. it will also produce outbound artifact logs that you can store locally for audit.
06:28 Priya Nair: encryption at rest — we need to validate KMS integration if we move to Private. is Redwood Private production-ready for SOC2/ISO needs?
06:40 Maya Delgado: Redwood Private is available and we have SOC2 Type II in our roadmap (or already achieved depending on product timeline). i'll attach our compliance pack and the Private deployment checklist.
06:52 Evan Torres: great. small wrinkle: our product team wants to do a cost-sensitivity test — can you simulate quantized runs vs float?
06:58 Ravi Shah: absolutely. harness will run model variants: fp16 baseline, 8-bit quant, and optimized kernels. we'll show per-model latency and cost delta. be aware quantization can slightly increase hallucination risk for very small keys; we'll track schema accuracy per variant.
07:20 Jordan Lee: on timelines — we need a pilot that can deliver a go/no-go recommendation for execs by July 20th. is that doable?
07:28 Maya Delgado: yes, that's about 6-7 weeks from now. fits the six-week plan: start mid-week, baseline in week 1, optimizations weeks 2-3, reliability week 4, exec summary week 6.
07:40 Samir Gupta: dependency list from our side: network diagram, KMS policy, traffic samples, and a contact to provision peering access. we'll deliver.
07:49 Maya Delgado: action items noted — i'll send the SOW + POC checklist and Ravi will push the harness repo.
07:55 Priya Nair: one more thing — tool calling latency, we want end-to-end (model decision + tool roundtrip) p95 under 1s. is that realistic with external enrichment calls?
08:05 Ravi Shah: that's tight but possible if tool calls are async and we pre-warm. we can model a proxy enrichment path inside the same VPC to eliminate cross-region latency. we'll show a table in the benchmark planning doc.
08:18 Evan Torres: any recommended guardrails to reduce hallucinations on structured outputs?
08:22 Lina Park: system prompts, function calling, response validators, and temperature control. for critical fields set temperature 0 and use function call enforcement. add a regeneration pass if the validator fails.
08:35 Jordan Lee: ok, next steps and wrap.
08:38 Maya Delgado: recap: 6-week pilot, bench harness, schema tests, quantization runs, hosted start then Private/Dedicated if needed. deliverables: SOW, harness link, sample config, and a kickoff slot.
08:51 Evan Torres: i'll get the traffic and KMS notes over. thanks everyone.
08:55 Maya Delgado: thanks— we'll send the docs and follow up; speak soon.
